title: An Ancient Wine-Making Site Was Found Beside an Egyptian Temple
mediaSource: Sekhmet Temple Memphis Egypt excavation wine press mud brick houses archaeology

scenes.title: Was wine being made beside an Egyptian temple?
scenes.narration: Near the Temple of Sekhmet in ancient Memphis, archaeologists found homes and a structure that may have been used to make wine.
keywords: Sekhmet Temple Memphis excavation real photo

scenes.title: Mud-brick houses and courtyards emerged
scenes.narration: A joint Egyptian-Chinese team uncovered a residential area near the temple with multiple mud-brick houses and courtyards.
keywords: ancient Egyptian mud brick houses excavation

scenes.title: A limestone structure moved liquid downward
scenes.narration: Nearby, archaeologists found a limestone installation with an upper basin sloping toward an opening and a lower basin designed to collect liquid.

scenes.title: Researchers think it may be a wine press
scenes.narration: Because of its shape and drainage system, researchers believe the installation may have been used to press grapes and collect juice for wine production.

scenes.title: Daily life continued beside the temple
scenes.narration: Pottery, amulets, small figurines, and written fragments were also found, showing that the area was not only religious but also a place where people lived and worked.

scenes.title: A temple neighborhood comes back to life
scenes.narration: The discovery reveals more than monumental architecture. Homes and production spaces show the everyday life that continued right beside one of ancient Memphis's sacred places.
